mcat_description.short: Portable houses are factory-built, transportable prefabricated structures with steel frames and insulated panel walls, sold as complete ready-to-use units or flat-pack kits for quick on-site assembly. They serve as temporary or semi-permanent dwellings, site offices, labour accommodation, and residential cabins across India.
mcat_description.long: A portable house is a prefabricated structure manufactured off-site — typically using cold-formed or mild steel frames combined with insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, or rock wool core) — and delivered as a complete unit or in modular components for rapid on-site assembly without conventional masonry. In the Indian B2B market, the dominant commercial form is a single-room or multi-room steel cabin used for construction site offices, labour accommodation, security posts, and temporary residential use, with standard floor dimensions quoted in feet (e.g., 10×10, 10×20, 20×40 ft). The category also encompasses capsule/pod houses, container-converted homes, wooden cabins, modular multi-storey units, and luxury prefab villas, all sharing the defining characteristic of factory fabrication and relocatability. Key buyer-facing attributes include insulation grade, structural frame material, floor area, number of rooms, weather resistance rating, and whether electrical/plumbing fittings are pre-installed.

market_context: The Indian portable/prefabricated house market is a fast-growing segment of the broader prefab construction industry, which stood at approximately USD 15 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow at 8.8% CAGR through 2030 (Mordor Intelligence). Modular buildings command the largest product share at 40.33%, while residential applications lead end-use at 52.1% of market value. The dominant commercial form in the Indian B2B market is a cold-formed steel frame structure with insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, or rock wool core), used primarily for construction site offices, labour accommodation, and temporary residential use — confirmed by major Indian manufacturers including EPACK Prefab, Tata Steel Nest-In, and Pressmach. The category spans a wide spectrum from basic single-room steel cabins (standard dimensions: 10×10 to 20×40 ft) to luxury modular villas and capsule/pod houses. Key demand drivers include government affordable housing schemes (PMAY), rising construction activity, labour welfare requirements at project sites, and growing interest in eco-resort and farmhouse applications. Steel frame compliance with BIS standards (IS 2062 for structural steel, IS 801 for cold-formed sections) is a buyer-cited quality signal. Major Indian players include EPACK Prefab, Tata Steel Nest-In, Loom Crafts, Pressmach, Everest Industries, and Larsen & Toubro. The capsule/pod house sub-segment is an emerging niche with notable keyword demand (692 impressions for 'capsule house'). Portable toilets are a sibling MCAT and must not be listed under this MCAT.
